## Problem description

This puzzle, published by Mickaël Launay [@lemonde2025dominos], reads as follows:

The problem is to tile the grid shown in the illustration below with dominoes, each covering two squares
(vertical or horizontal), such that:

- the dominoes do not overlap;

- every domino either covers a star or is adjacent to a domino that covers a star.

Two dominoes are considered adjacent if they share a side, but not if they touch only at a corner.

![Illustration from [@lemonde2025dominos]](images/star_dominoes.png){width=30% fig-align="center"}


## MIP model

#### Parameters

- $C$: set of cells of the grid
- $P$: set of candidate dominoes. A domino $p\in P$ is defined as a "subgrid" of the grid; 
therefore it is defined not only by its shape, but also by the set of cells it covers. 
- $P^*\subset P$: set of dominoes which cover a star
- $S(p)\subset P^*$: set of adjacent dominoes of $p\not\in P^*$ which cover a star

#### Variables

- $\textcolor{blue}{x}_{p} \in \{0,1\}$: takes value $1$ if and only if domino $p\in P$ is used

#### Objective function

As this is a feasibility problem, any dummy objective function is suitable:

$$
\min 0
$$

subject to:

#### Constraints

- A cell of the grid must be covered exactly once 
by one of the candidate polyominoes (no overlapping):

\begin{align}
\sum_{p \in P|c \in p}\textcolor{blue}{x}_{p}= 1 \quad \forall c \in C \\
\end{align}

- If a domino that does not cover a start is selected, one of its adjacent 
dominoes covering a start must also be selected:

$$
\textcolor{blue}{x}_{p} \le \sum_{q \in S(p)}\textcolor{blue}{x}_{q} \quad \forall p \not \in P^*
$$
